newsitem.title: MEXICO: Outcomes still shifting from Mexico's July 6 vote.
newsitem.headline: Outcomes still shifting from Mexico's July 6 vote.

text.p: Mexican election authorities said on Wednesday they would overturn results from one tight congressional race to favour the ruling party and annul results from a second district where ballot boxes were burned.
Nonetheless, irregularities from the landmark July 6 congressional elections were "minimal," the Electoral Tribunal said.
Voting was annulled at 1.07 percent of the country's 104,584 polling stations, mostly because of technicalities and not because of attempts at fraud, the tribunal said.
"This confirms that in the 1997 federal elections, irregularities were minimal," Jose Luis de la Peza, president of the tribunal, told reporters.

The July 6 vote was widely hailed as the freest and fairest in 68 years of rule by the Institutional Ruling Party (PRI), which lost its absolute majority in the lower house of Congress for the first time.
The PRI has a checkered electoral history, sometimes resorting to outright fraud to remain in power.
The Electoral Tribunal is a multiparty panel that determines the outcome of federal elections. Voting results are not final as political parties have until Aug. 19 to appeal any rulings.
The tribunal has until Aug. 22 to close its books on the elections.
The tribunal said it had ruled the PRI a winner in a congressional district in central Guanajuato state that had originally been granted to the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD).
Some voting boxes were thrown out on technicalities, shifting the outcome to the PRI, the tribunal said.
The PRD immediately said it would challenge that ruling and others, including a decision by Campeche state election officials to award the governor's race there to the PRI.
The PRD alleges massive PRI fraud in Campeche, including the fabrication of false ballots.
The annulled congressional election took place in a district in the southern state of Chiapas that is the bedrock of support for the Zapatista armed guerrilla movement.
People in the town of Ocosingo burned ballot boxes on election day, invalidating the outcome. A new election will be held for that district, but the date has not been set.

According to preliminary results, the PRI won 239 of the 500 seats in the lower house of Congress while the PRD took 125 and the conservative National Action Party (PAN) 122. Two minor parties split the rest.
If the latest tribunal rulings hold up, the PRI's total would stand at 239, the PRD would lose one to fall to 124 and one district would remain open pending the rerun election.
